---
title: "Guard the Door"
---

::: {.quest-dialog}
- **Goal:** You will write a hook that refuses a command, and know where a hook's coverage ends.
- **Before you start:** [Plug In a Server](plug-in-a-server.html). An **exit code** is the number a script returns when it finishes: 0 means success, and a hook uses 2 to mean "block". **JSON** is a structured text format.
- **Time:** about 15 minutes.
:::

A **hook** is a user-defined handler that runs automatically at a set point in the harness's lifecycle. In Claude Code it can be a shell command, an HTTP endpoint and other kinds, and it receives JSON about the event. An instructions file asks the model to behave. A command hook is ordinary code that the harness runs, so what it decides does not depend on what the model wants.

## A hook that refuses

::: {.panel-tabset group="companion"}

## Claude Code

Hooks go in a `hooks` block in a settings file:

- `.claude/settings.json`: committable and shared.
- `.claude/settings.local.json`: yours alone.
- `~/.claude/settings.json`: all projects.

A `PreToolUse` hook fires before a tool runs, and the matcher (the pattern that selects which tool the hook fires for) `Bash` selects the shell tool:

```json
{ "hooks": { "PreToolUse": [ { "matcher": "Bash",
  "hooks": [ { "type": "command",
    "command": "\"$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR\"/.claude/hooks/block-drop-table.sh" } ] } ] } }
```

The script, from the Claude Code hooks guide. It needs `jq` installed to read the JSON, and it must be executable (`chmod +x` is the usual way):

```bash
#!/bin/bash
INPUT=$(cat)
COMMAND=$(echo "$INPUT" | jq -r '.tool_input.command')
if echo "$COMMAND" | grep -q "drop table"; then
  echo "Blocked: dropping tables is not allowed" >&2  # stderr becomes Claude's feedback
  exit 2                                               # exit 2 = block the action
fi
exit 0  # exit 0 = no decision; the normal permission flow applies
```

The hook gets the event as JSON on stdin (its standard input), including `tool_name` and, for Bash, `tool_input.command`. Exit code 2 on `PreToolUse` blocks the call, and Claude sees the stderr text (the program's error output) as the reason. Exit 0 expresses no decision: the call goes through the normal permission flow.

Two behaviours matter for trust:

- **A broken guard fails open.** If the script crashes or exits with some other code and prints no valid JSON, the action proceeds on most events. To block on failure, configure the hook for it (the hooks guide names `onFailure: "block"`; check the hooks reference for where it goes).
- **Exit 2 blocks on some events only.** On `PostToolUse` the tool already ran and exit 2 shows stderr to Claude. On `Notification` the exit code is ignored.

## OpenCode + Ollama

The V2 docs describe plugins (files under `.opencode/plugins/` or `~/.config/opencode/plugins/`) that can register hooks. To refuse an action, use the permission hook, `ctx.permission.hook("evaluate", ...)`: it runs for `allow` and `ask` decisions, may change the effect to `allow`, `ask` or `deny`, and `event.message` is the denial reason. An explicit configured `deny` is final and never invokes the hook.

Treat an OpenCode plugin as code running with your privileges. Before relying on it, check your installed version's docs for shell-hook configuration and an exit-code equivalent, and test whether throwing from a tool hook blocks a call. Test the whole setup with your local Ollama model too.

:::

## What a hook covers

- **A string match is easy to dodge.** The example matches the literal string "drop table" in one command. A matcher selects by tool name, not by content. If the model runs a script that contains the dangerous command, or spells it differently, a grep on the command text never sees it.
- **Hooks fire only on tool calls.** `PreToolUse` fires when Claude calls a tool. A file added with an `@` reference in your prompt is read without a tool call, so no hook fires.
- **Hooks cannot override your deny and ask rules.** A hook returning allow skips the prompt, and deny and ask rules are still evaluated.
- **Hooks run with your full permissions.** Command hooks "execute shell commands with your full user permissions", so review and test them before adding them.

## One door for the high-stakes actions

If an agent can reach something with real-world consequences, such as ordering DNA synthesis or commanding physical equipment, put a screening checkpoint in the path that refuses dual-use requests (requests where the same capability can help or harm). Do not connect an agent to such a capability without one. Test the checkpoint with requests you know it should refuse. A hook is one possible checkpoint for local actions, with the limits listed above.

## A hook in a repository is code you did not write

If a repository commits hooks in `.claude/settings.json`, they are code from its authors, running as you. Interactive Claude Code holds hooks back until you accept the workspace trust dialog.

In `-p` and SDK runs (headless: non-interactive, no one to answer a dialog) there is no dialog, and hooks committed in a repository's `.claude/settings.json` run in a folder you have never trusted. Read `.claude/` before running headless in a clone. `--bare` and `disableAllHooks` switch hooks off.

<div data-ao-honour="gatehouse-hook-in-a-scratch-folder" data-xp="20">In a throwaway folder with mock files, add the Bash-blocking hook above and ask for a harmless command that contains "drop table" in an `echo`. Note the stderr message the agent reports. Then change the script to exit 1 and see what happens.</div>

*Further reading. Optional.*

- [AI for Science, practice 10: screen for dual-use and high-consequence risk](https://aiforscience.eu/best-practices/10-screen-dual-use-high-consequence/): AI for Science (European draft best practices), docs. Why read: it describes one screening checkpoint for high-consequence actions and tested refusals. A draft with no endorsements yet; it is aimed mostly at providers and institutions.
- [Hooks reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks): Anthropic, docs. Why read: it lists the hook events, handler types and the exit-code rules, including exit 2 to block.
- [Configure permissions](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions): Anthropic, docs. Why read: it covers deny and ask rules, which still apply when a hook says allow.
- [Best practices for Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices): Anthropic, docs. Why read: it says when to reach for a PreToolUse hook instead of an instruction.
